decisions.reason: Although no longer highlighted on the website, this adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display remains close to the firm's core offer, so without a clear performance shortfall below aspiration management would likely keep it as a flexible variant.
This pegboard-backed cardboard display fits existing capabilities and customer needs well, so a large firm with some slack would usually retain it unless internal results have clearly disappointed.
As a fairly standard quarter-pallet cardboard display with overlap to other core products and no recent visibility, it is more likely to be rationalised if its results have settled below aspiration.

The wooden display pallet is less aligned with the paper-based core business and likely harder to justify if margins or demand have not matched aspiration levels, so resources would probably be reallocated.
Its media-specific niche narrows demand, and after several years without stronger signs of success management would likely shift resources to broader core displays or new development.
